help.pageSubtitle: What to do when something goes wrong in Passport — common fixes before you contact support.
help.contactBody: If these steps do not resolve the issue, email support with your shipment reference, a short description, and screenshots if possible. Signed-in users can also send in-app feedback.
help.disclaimer: Passport provides assistive trade-compliance tools. Outputs are not legal or customs advice. For binding decisions, consult qualified counsel or your licensed customs broker.

signIn.title: Can't sign in
steps: Confirm you are using the email address your organization registered with.
Check for typos in your password; passwords are case-sensitive.
If you were invited to a shipment, use the link in the invitation email to sign up or accept first.
Try signing out completely, clearing the browser tab, and signing in again.
If you still cannot access your account, email support from the address on your account.

documents.title: Document upload or processing failed
documents.summary: Files stuck on pending, processing, or failed extraction.
steps: Open the shipment and check the Documents section for a status badge and any error message.
Processing runs in the background — wait 1–2 minutes and refresh the page.
Use PDF or clear images (PNG/JPEG). Very large files may take longer.
If status is failed, open the document detail page and retry processing if available.
Re-upload a cleaner copy if the original scan is blurry or truncated.
Check that required parties and products exist on the shipment before expecting full verification.

blocked.title: Shipment blocked or low Passport Score
blocked.summary: Readiness is not met for clearance handoff.
steps: Open the shipment and review the Passport Score card for the lowest-scoring dimensions.
Resolve open discrepancies — mismatched quantities, dates, or party names between documents.
Upload missing document types flagged in the documentation checklist.
Complete or assign open workflow tasks from verification and regulatory results.
Use Clearance readiness to see organization-wide blockers across shipments.
When score and checks look good, use Confirm ready (owner/broker flow) if your role allows.

verification.title: Verification discrepancies
steps: Open Discrepancies on the shipment — read each item's expected vs. found values.
Fix source documents and re-upload, or update shipment parties/products if the shipment record was wrong.
Resolve items you have corrected; ignore only when you have documented justification.
Re-run verification after document changes (use Verify on the shipment if shown).
Check Compliance alerts for critical items affecting multiple shipments.

regulatory.title: Regulatory checks failing
regulatory.summary: Compliance rules flagged missing permits, documents, or restrictions.
steps: Open Regulatory / compliance checks on the shipment and read each failed rule.
Upload the required document type or obtain the permit/registration cited in the rule.
Confirm origin, destination, and product category on the shipment match your trade lane.
Re-run regulatory checks after uploading new documents.
Remember: Passport rules are assistive — confirm requirements with your broker or authority.

invites.title: Collaboration invite not working
invites.summary: Broker, forwarder, or external collaborator cannot access a shipment.
steps: Open the invitation link from email — it may require sign-up first for external collaborators.
Confirm the invite was sent to the correct email address.
Ask the shipment owner to resend the invite from the shipment Collaborators panel.
Ensure the invite has not expired; request a new one if needed.
After accepting, sign out and back in if the shipment does not appear immediately.

inbound.title: Email or WhatsApp document not appearing
inbound.summary: Inbound channel ingestion did not create or attach a document.
steps: Open Settings → Channels and confirm the inbound email address or WhatsApp number.
Send from the email or phone number registered on your profile or channel settings.
Include the shipment reference in the subject or message body when possible.
Attach trade documents as PDF or image files — not only links.
Allow a few minutes for processing, then refresh the shipment documents list.
If nothing arrives after 15 minutes, upload manually and contact support with the sent timestamp.

api.title: API or webhook errors
steps: Confirm your API key is active under Settings → API keys.
Send the Authorization header as documented in Settings → API docs.
For webhooks, verify the endpoint URL is reachable (HTTPS in production) and returns 2xx.
Check Settings → Webhooks → deliveries for failure payloads and response codes.
Rotate keys if you suspect leakage; update integrations with the new key.
Rate limits may apply — backoff and retry on 429 responses.

howItWorks.title: How Passport works
howItWorks.subtitle: Four steps from fragmented documents to clearance-ready shipments.

step1.title: Create a shipment
step1.description: Set your trade corridor, parties, and product lines. Passport organizes everything in one tenant-secure workspace.

step2.title: Upload documents
step2.description: Drop PDFs or images — or ingest via email and WhatsApp channels. AI classifies and extracts key fields.

step3.title: Verify & comply
step3.description: Run cross-document checks and regulatory rules. Resolve discrepancies and workflow tasks with full audit history.

step4.title: Hand off to clearance
step4.description: Confirm readiness, share with your broker, and export compliance reports when you're satisfied — not when customs finds the gap.
